items.title: An Android and iOS app from 7 Claude Code commands, every prompt and timing
items.why_it_matters: A developer documented how they built a complete cross-platform app using just seven Claude Code commands, showing the exact prompts and timing. This is a practical masterclass in the "direction" part of vibe coding that you are trying to master. Try running a similar structured sequence of prompts in Claude Code today to scaffold a new feature or clean up your AI-ingest codebase.

items.title: Show HN: I built a Chrome extension so Claude can close my 300 tabs
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer built and shipped Tab Genie, a Chrome extension that uses Claude to categorize and close browser tabs. It is a great example of a simple, single-purpose AI tool shipped to production. You can look at how they structured their categorization prompts and apply a similar logic to filter the news items in your AI-ingest project this week.

items.title: Show HN: Echologue – the private AI voice journal I built for myself
items.why_it_matters: A developer built and shipped Echologue, a private, voice-first AI journaling app that automatically tags and retrieves entries using local embeddings. It shows how a solo developer can build a highly polished, personal AI utility. Try implementing a simple semantic search or tagging feature in your Next.js/Supabase stack this week using Supabase's built-in vector support.

items.title: Show HN: Tokimeter – open-source usage meter for Claude, Codex, Cursor and more
items.why_it_matters: Tokimeter is a new open-source tool that tracks your token usage and costs across Claude, Codex, and other coding assistants. Since you are vibe coding daily, keeping an eye on your token spend is crucial to avoid surprise bills. Install Tokimeter today to start tracking exactly how many tokens your AI-ingest development is consuming.

items.title: Show HN: ClaudeFS – Give claude.ai access to a local folder, no local process
items.why_it_matters: ClaudeFS is a new tool that gives the web-based Claude.ai interface access to a local folder without requiring a complex local setup. This is incredibly useful if you want to use the web UI's visual capabilities alongside your terminal workflow. Try installing ClaudeFS this week to easily feed a Next.js component file from your local repo into the Claude web interface for a quick UI redesign.
